Staffordshire Moorlands' population decreased by around 1,300 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

Staffordshire Moorlands' population decreased

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Staffordshire Moorlands fell by 1.3%, from just over 97,100 in 2011 to around 95,800 in 2021.

This means Staffordshire Moorlands was one of only two local authority areas in the West Midlands to see its population decline. The regional population increased by 6.2%, while the population of England increased by 6.6%.

In 2021, Staffordshire Moorlands was home to around 1.2 people per football pitch-sized piece of land. This area was among the lowest 20% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

The population of Staffordshire Moorlands decreased by around 1.3%

An older Staffordshire Moorlands

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Staffordshire Moorlands increased by four years, from 45 to 49 years of age.

This area had the second-highest average (median) age in the West Midlands (behind Malvern Hills) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 75 to 84 years rose by around 2,200 (an increase of 33.6%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 5,100 (24.1% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 75 and 84 years increased by 2.4 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Staffordshire Moorlands residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 91,800 Staffordshire Moorlands residents said they were born in England. This represented 95.8% of the local population. The figure has decreased from around 93,100 in 2011, which at the time represented 95.9% of Staffordshire Moorlands' population.

Wales was the next most represented, with around 750 Staffordshire Moorlands residents reporting this country of birth (0.8%). This figure was down from around 800 in 2011, which at the time also represented 0.8% of the population of Staffordshire Moorlands.

The number of Staffordshire Moorlands residents born in Scotland fell from around 750 in 2011 (0.8% of the local population) to around 650 in 2021 (0.7%).

In 2021, 95.8% of Staffordshire Moorlands residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in Staffordshire Moorlands

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in nearby East Staffordshire (3.8 percentage points) than in Staffordshire Moorlands (0.3 percentage points).

In Staffordshire Moorlands, the percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity stayed close to 1.5% between the last two censuses. During the same period, the percentage in nearby East Staffordshire increased from 5.5% to 9.3%.

The percentage of people who identified with a UK and non-UK national identity in Staffordshire Moorlands increased from 0.2% to 0.5%, while the percentage of people who identified as "British only" increased from 12.9% to 56.5%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Staffordshire Moorlands increased by 0.3 percentage points

Rise in private renting

In 2021, 12.7% of Staffordshire Moorlands households rented privately. This figure increased from 9.8% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 12 households (8.6%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 8.9% in 2011. The percentage of Staffordshire Moorlands households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 79.7% to 78.2%.

This area had the region’s joint third lowest percentage of privately-rented homes (alongside Lichfield). Across the region, only South Staffordshire (10.6%) and Bromsgrove (10.6%) had a lower percentage of privately-rented homes.

Private renting in Staffordshire Moorlands increased by 2.9 percentage points

Unpaid care in Staffordshire Moorlands

In 2021, 5.5% of Staffordshire Moorlands residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 8.5% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.8%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.6% in 2011. The proportion of Staffordshire Moorlands residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care decreased from 2.8% to 2.7%.

This area had the country's third highest proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care. Across the country, only Isles of Scilly (5.6%) and Gedling (5.6%) had a higher proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care.

Because of its small size, comparisons to Isles of Scilly should be made with caution.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Staffordshire Moorlands decreased by 3.0 percentage points

Religion in Staffordshire Moorlands

In 2021, 33.9% of Staffordshire Moorlands residents reported having "No religion", up from 19.6% in 2011. The rise of 14.3 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Staffordshire Moorlands. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 22.0% to 32.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 59.3% of people in Staffordshire Moorlands described themselves as Christian (down from 72.8%), while 5.7% did not state their religion (down from 6.8% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 33.9% of usual residents in Staffordshire Moorlands reported having "No religion"

Fall in employment

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Staffordshire Moorlands (2.9 percentage points) than across England (0.8 percentage points).

In Staffordshire Moorlands, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) decreased from 57.3% in 2011 to 54.4% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage across England decreased from 56.5% to 55.7%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Staffordshire Moorlands fell from 2.5% to 1.6%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) increased from 27.2% to 30.3%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Staffordshire Moorlands decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 10.2% of Staffordshire Moorlands residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 9.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in eight people (13.0%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 14.8% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 55.9% to 56.9%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was greater in Staffordshire Moorlands (0.7 percentage points) than across the West Midlands (0.3 percentage points, from 9.6% to 9.9%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Staffordshire Moorlands increased by 0.7 percentage points

Family in Staffordshire Moorlands

In 2021, 7.5% of Staffordshire Moorlands households included a couple with only non-dependent children. This figure decreased from 8.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in six households (17.3%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 19.3% in 2011. The percentage of single-family households including a couple without children decreased from 20.8% to 19.4%.

Staffordshire Moorlands saw the West Midlands' joint second-largest fall (alongside Lichfield) in the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children. This area had the region’s tenth highest percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children.

The percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children in Staffordshire Moorlands decreased by 0.5 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Staffordshire Moorlands

In 2021, 0.9% of Staffordshire Moorlands residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 0.6% in 2011. The 0.3 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 2.4% to 3.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 98.0% of people in Staffordshire Moorlands identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 98.7% in 2011), while 0.7% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 0.5% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.1% in 2011 to 0.2% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 0.9% of usual residents in Staffordshire Moorlands identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Staffordshire Moorlands residents aged 16 years and over, 29.4% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 26.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in two people (51.3%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 54.2% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Staffordshire Moorlands that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.8% to 9.3%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater across the West Midlands (3.4 percentage points, from 33.7% to 37.1%) than in Staffordshire Moorlands (2.8 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Staffordshire Moorlands increased by 2.8 percentage points

Disability in Staffordshire Moorlands

In 2021, 7.4% of Staffordshire Moorlands residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 9.4% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.3%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 10.5% in 2011. The proportion of Staffordshire Moorlands residents who were not disabled increased from 80.2% to 82.3%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Staffordshire Moorlands (2.0 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the West Midlands (1.9 percentage points, from 9.9% to 8.0%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Staffordshire Moorlands decreased by 2.0 percentage points

Health in Staffordshire Moorlands

In 2021, 48.3% of Staffordshire Moorlands residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 46.1% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" remained at 34.4%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Staffordshire Moorlands residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.1% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 4.3% to 3.7%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Staffordshire Moorlands increased by 2.2 percentage points
